A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECLipsE-Gen-Local. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables and complete appendices can be matched reliably, including the additional material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Lipschitz estimates and computation times on generated networks, input-radius sensitivity experiments, and MNIST robustness evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and additionally reports certified robustness radii for 20 MNIST points in Appendix A.3.5.

M1.justification: The Acc, Fast and CF procedures, slope refinement, affine-layer acceleration and numerical safeguards remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–5. The correction to Equation (12) aligns its indexing with the terminal step already used in v1's pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate generated ReLU/ELU networks, shrinking input regions for LeakyReLU networks, and standard versus Jacobian-regularized MNIST classifiers. The added certified-radius analysis reuses the existing MNIST points and perturbation scales.

E2.justification: The scalability benchmark comparator set is retained. Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3.5 newly compare local-bound robustness certificates against certificates from the global trivial bound, introducing that comparator into the MNIST certification analysis.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds a certified-radius evaluation: compute the logit-margin radius, cap it by the region where the local bound is valid, and maximize across eight existing perturbation scales. Existing training, network configurations and PGD settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The added MNIST robustness-certificate analysis examines how local Lipschitz estimates translate into guaranteed label-invariant radii across input scales. This extends v1's comparison with empirical attack failures; the existing depth, width and input-radius analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across 20 input points in Figure 6. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing changes are introduced; the new radius means add results without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix A.3.5 adds certified radii with means 0.01222977 locally versus 0.001990887 using the trivial bound, a reported ratio of 6.14. Table 1b also changes ECLipsE-Fast's 5-layer, 10-neuron runtime from 0.020 to 0.002 seconds. Other existing tabulated results match.

T1.justification: Equation (12) corrects its cases from i in Z_N and i=N−1 to i in Z_(N−1) and i=N. Section 4.3 adds the local-radius certificate and validity argument, while Appendix A.4 explicitly identifies the discarded CF matrix term. Existing Appendix A.1 proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims of scalable, certified local Lipschitz estimation, flexible input-output selection and tight small-region bounds are retained. The rewritten fourth contribution emphasizes existing Theorems 3 and 6; CNN and residual-network extensions remain prospective.

C2.justification: v2 adds practical variant-selection guidance, explains when cheaper global estimation is preferable, and discusses when CF slope relaxation introduces substantial conservatism. It also explains the rationale for comparing split LipSDP with full-network ECLipsE-Gen-Local.

D1.justification: v2 adds Python package eclipse-nn and PyPI installation/access information to its code disclosure; v1 provides a MATLAB-subdirectory code link. Hardware, network generation, training and attack details in Appendix A.3.1–A.3.3 are retained.

R1.justification: Six citations are added to motivate applications in neural control, power-flow surrogates, early-exit networks, encoder-decoder structures and multitask models. The positioning relative to earlier Lipschitz-estimation methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the fourth contribution, adds explanatory remarks and appendix subsections, and makes wording corrections such as '20 neurons' to '20 layers' in the depth discussion. The main section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the certified-radii table, publication headers and lighter table rules, and reflows existing figures and algorithms. The Figure 4 caption/body overlap on v1 page 18 is resolved in v2; the existing plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical validation by adding explicit MNIST robustness certificates where v1 only related Lipschitz estimates to attack failures. Corrected indexing, clearer applicability and conservatism discussions, and Python package information improve correctness and usability. The gain is limited because the added evaluation reuses the same 20 points and the central method and coverage remain unchanged.
